LESSON: INDIGENOUS KENYAN GAMES

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.6: Indigenous Kenyan Games
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 15

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Indigenous Kenyan Games, part of Creating and Performing in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade five CREATIVE ARTS.

Key inquiry question: How do indigenous counting games enhance physical fitness? 2. Why indigenous counting games are considered indigenous?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. identify types of indigenous counting games played in Kenya,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan Games in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. perform different indigenous counting games for skill acquisition,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan Games in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform indigenous counting games to a musical rhythm for enjoyment,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan Games in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. appreciate the role played by counting games for fitness and health.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Indigenous Kenyan Games in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. perform indigenous counting games to a musical rhythm for enjoyment,

D. appreciate the role played by counting games for fitness and health.

E. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

2. demonstrate indigenous counting games while observing safety, Learners with postural defects could use alternative functional parts of the body, perform an alternative corresponding activity, or perform at their level of functional ability. Safety of all learners should be 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Indigenous Kenyan Games together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Values:
 Responsibility: The learner takes on different roles during indigenous counting games.

 Unity: The learner works with others in indigenous counting games.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

 Health and Fitness: The learner improves fitness through indigenous counting games for a healthy lifestyle.

 Mathematics: The learner keeps counting during indigenous counting games.
